title: --iex is offered on the language axis but read by exactly one built-in
body:
# 0009: --iex is offered on the language axis but read by exactly one built-in

## Tags

help, activation, options, D11, D20, recurrence-of-0001

## Summary

`--iex` is advertised as a shared option in every project that declares `elixir`, and its summary says it starts "the surface" in IEx. Exactly one thing in devbin reads `DEVBIN_OPT_IEX`: the built-in `server` handler. So the flag is inert for `cli` and `repl` in every project, and inert entirely in a project that declares elixir and disables `server` -- which is both of the second fleet's installed projects so far.

This is issue 0001's deferred question 2, now answered by evidence rather than by argument. 0001 asked whether the right activation key is the language or the consuming command, chose the language because "with exactly one framework option, the simpler one is probably right", and left the sharper answer to D18's tier-4 discipline: do not generalise ahead of the evidence. `lib/resolve:725-730` records the assumption in as many words -- "the language and the consumer set are the same thing today". They are no longer the same thing.

Found while authoring arca_config's `cli` help topic in ST0002 WP-02, by writing down what the flag does and then checking it.

## Reproduction

Two faces, both real.

**Face 1 -- offered where nothing at all can read it.** arca_config and MicroGPTEx both declare `elixir` and both set `commands.server.enabled: false`.

    $ bin/ac help
    Shared options (after the command):
      --iex                 Start the surface in IEx rather than plain

    $ bin/ac help --why
      iex                   Interactive Elixir shell with the project loaded
      --iex                 Start the surface in IEx rather than plain

No line anywhere says the flag is unavailable, and `server` is not in the offered list at all. This is 0001's own screen, one layer down: 0001 was the shell-project case where the LANGUAGE was absent, and its fix covered exactly that.

**Face 2 -- offered correctly, and still inert for two of the three surfaces.** Proven with a poisoned `iex` first on PATH, in arca_config:

    $ PATH=<poison>:$PATH bin/ac cli --version      # control
    A simple file-based configurator for Elixir apps 0.3.0
    $ PATH=<poison>:$PATH bin/ac cli --iex --version
    A simple file-based configurator for Elixir apps 0.3.0   # byte-identical, poison never fired
    $ PATH=<poison>:$PATH bin/ac iex
    POISON-IEX-FIRED: -S mix                                 # the builtin command does invoke it

`grep -c DEVBIN_OPT_IEX lib/cmd/cli` is 0, and `lib/cmd/repl` likewise. `grep -rln DEVBIN_OPT_IEX lib/cmd/` returns `lib/cmd/server` and nothing else. Face 2 is true in all six projects, including the whole first fleet, and has been since D20 landed.

## Root Cause

The gap is where two mechanisms meet, not inside either one -- the same sentence 0001 closes on.

D20 made `--iex` framework-owned so a shipped handler could read a canonical name. 0001 then wired the option's OFFER to the declared language (`_DEVBIN_FRAMEWORK_OPTIONS="iex:elixir"`, `lib/resolve:731`), because at the time every elixir project in the corpus enabled `server`, so "language declared" and "some offered command consumes it" selected the same set. Neither statement was ever the other, and the second fleet is where they come apart: a library has no server to run.

Face 2 was never covered by any activation rule, because it is not an activation question. The option's SUMMARY -- "Start the surface in IEx rather than plain" -- generalises over surfaces that do not implement it. `lib/cmd/server`'s own header states the correct doctrine ("A framework option selects which command line runs; it does not transform one"), which is precisely why `cli` and `repl` cannot inherit the behaviour for free: each consuming handler has to implement its own two command lines, and only one of the three ever did.

## Impact

Worse than 0001, which was explicitly "cosmetic in effect". This one produced a false record in a migration.

ST0002 WP-02 retired `scripts/iex` (`iex -S mix Arca.Config`) and recorded its replacement as `bin/ac cli --iex`. The equivalence table proved that `mix Arca.Config` and `mix arca.config` resolve to the same module -- true, and not the claim at risk. The flag itself was never run. The script was then deleted in `2522cfb` on the strength of a disposition that does not work.

No capability was actually lost: the built-in `iex` command (`iex -S mix`) provides it, and arca_config's config comment, inventory and help now say so. The cost was a wrong reason recorded in three places, which is the failure mode "a conclusion can be right for the wrong reason" describes -- except here the conclusion was wrong too.

The general cost stands: `bin/<prj> cli --iex` is accepted, exported and ignored in six projects. A flag that is parsed and does nothing is the false-green shape at the option level.

## Proposed Fix

Filed rather than fixed. D20 is hv-ratified, 0001's fix was hv's call, and this changes the same behaviour, so the ruling is hv's.

**Face 1, recommended: key the offer on the consuming command, not the language.** `_DEVBIN_FRAMEWORK_OPTIONS` gains a consumer column (`iex:elixir:server`), and `_framework_option` offers the flag only when at least one consuming command is itself offered. This is the option 0001 named as "more precisely true" and deferred for want of evidence; the evidence is now two projects. It reuses the D11 activation already in place and adds no second mechanism.

**Face 2, needs a ruling, and it is the more interesting half.** Either:

1. **Narrow the claim.** The summary becomes specific about what reads it (`Start the server in IEx rather than plain`), and `--iex` is refused rather than ignored when passed to a command that does not consume it. Silent acceptance is what let WP-02 record a working disposition; a refusal would have failed loudly the first time it was typed. This matches the no-silent-errors rule and the zero-work promotions ruling.

2. **Widen the implementation.** `lib/cmd/cli` and `lib/cmd/repl` each grow their own two command lines, so `--iex` means something everywhere it is offered. For `cli` that is `iex -S mix <name>.cli` -- but note this changes what `cli` IS (one-shot, exits) into something that does not exit, and the project that wants that already has the `iex` command. Widening looks like the generous answer and is probably the wrong one.

The recommendation is Face 1 plus Face 2 option 1: make the offer honest, and make the flag loud where it is not implemented. Whatever is decided lands in D20 itself, not only in this issue -- the WP-09 `list` lesson, which 0001 also closes on.

## Resolution

**hv's ruling, 2026-08-10: `--iex` selects a SERVER's IEx form.** It is not a general "do this in IEx" modifier -- running `cli` or `repl` under it makes no sense and nobody would want to. Face 1 plus Face 2 option 1, as recommended, with one addition the survey forced.

**Lamplight is why the consumer set is extensible.** `bin/.devbin/cmd/wrighter` is a PROJECT handler that reads `DEVBIN_OPT_IEX` and picks a different command line for it -- so the consumer set is not "the built-in `server`" and never was. A framework table naming `server` alone would have refused `lamplight wrighter --iex`, a real and working invocation. Devbin knows its own consumers and cannot know a project's, so the project names them.

As built:

- `_DEVBIN_FRAMEWORK_OPTIONS` gains a consumer column (`iex:elixir:server`), and `_framework_option` offers the option only when one of its consumers is ACTIVE -- language AND consumer, not language as a proxy for consumer.
- `options.<name>.commands` extends the set with a project's own handlers. Lamplight needs `commands: [wrighter]` at its next upgrade or `wrighter --iex` is refused. Recorded as a migration obligation, not left to be discovered.
- The flag is REFUSED where the command cannot read it, through the dispatcher's existing "not available here" wording and exit 2, with the reason naming the commands that do take it.
- `_shared_option_declares_shape` splits "config mentions this option" from "config declares its shape". Without it, declaring only `commands:` flipped the framework flag into a valued option and `--iex` began eating the next argument -- caught by a test written for exactly that, not by luck.
- The summary reads "Start the server in IEx rather than plain". "The surface" is what made the flag read as universal.

The ruling landed in D20 itself (`intent/st/COMPLETED/ST0001/design.md`, "As built, 2026-08-10"), not only here -- the WP-09 `list` lesson that 0001 also closes on.

**The fleet is NOT re-vendored by this commit.** Devbin's own suite is the gate; the six installed projects keep the lib they have until their next upgrade, and Lamplight's config line has to land in the same operation as its re-vendor.

## Notes

Both faces are invisible to the gate: nothing fails, nothing seals red, `doctor` is 9/0. The only instrument that catches this class is writing down what a thing does and then running it -- which is what a help topic is.
